title: Washington's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: Washington's 2nd Congressional District covers Island, San Juan, Skagit, and Whatcom counties, plus western Snohomish County. Incumbent Democrat Rick Larsen, first elected in 2000, is seeking a 14th term in this safely Democratic district, which has a Cook PVI of D+12 and has not elected a Republican since 1998. Larsen faces four primary challengers: two Democrats (Devin Hermanson and Tomas Scheel) who criticize him as too moderate and tied to corporate donors, and two Republicans (Edwin Feller and Raymond Pelletti). The top-two primary will be held August 4, 2026, with the general election on November 3, 2026. If Democrats retake the House, Larsen is poised to chair the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.
polling_note: No opinion polls were found for this race. All major nonpartisan analysts (Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball) rate the seat as 'Solid D' or 'Safe D.'

candidates.name: Rick Larsen
candidates.summary: Rick Larsen is the Democratic incumbent representing Washington's 2nd Congressional District since 2001. He serves on the House Armed Services and Transportation and Infrastructure committees and would chair the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee if Democrats retake the House. Larsen has raised over $1.6 million for his re-election campaign as of March 2026 and has been endorsed by numerous local elected officials across all five counties in the district.

candidates.name: Devin Hermanson
candidates.summary: Devin Hermanson is a Democratic candidate challenging incumbent Rick Larsen from the left. He is a media consultant, filmmaker, and founder of MOYO Media Lab who has also worked at Microsoft and World Vision. Hermanson previously ran for this seat in 2024 and refuses to accept any campaign donations, relying instead on grassroots organizing. His platform includes the Green New Deal, Medicare for All, and substantial campaign finance reform.

candidates.name: Tomas Scheel
candidates.summary: Tomas Scheel is a Democratic candidate running as a progressive challenger to Rick Larsen. He is a U.S. Air Force veteran and small business owner who builds software systems in Whatcom County. Scheel refuses corporate PAC money and advocates for accountability, anti-corruption measures, uniform code of public servant justice, AI legislation, and healthcare reform. He is the son of an Ecuadorian immigrant mother and an American union tradesman father.

candidates.name: Edwin H. Feller
candidates.summary: Edwin H. Feller is a Republican candidate running for Congress in Washington's 2nd District. A lifelong Lynden resident born on his family's farm, Feller is an 83-year-old HVAC contractor who spent much of his career working overseas on U.S. government construction projects, including embassies in 60 countries. This is his first run for political office, and he is running on a platform of robust law enforcement, border security, nuclear and hydroelectric energy expansion, and immigration reform prioritizing nuclear families.

candidates.name: Raymond Pelletti
candidates.summary: Raymond Pelletti is a Republican candidate from Blaine, Washington, running for Congress in the 2nd District. He previously ran for Washington State House of Representatives in the 42nd Legislative District in 2024, advancing to the general election against incumbent Democrat Alicia Rule. Pelletti is one of two Republicans in the five-candidate primary field challenging incumbent Democrat Rick Larsen.

forecast.rationale: No public polls exist for this race, capping confidence at medium. However, all available structural indicators point to an overwhelming Democratic advantage: Cook PVI of D+12, no Republican victory in the district since 1998, and uniform ratings of 'Solid D' / 'Safe D' from Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball. Incumbent Rick Larsen has held the seat since 2001, raised over $1.6 million, and has broad bipartisan-county endorsements. The Republican field consists of two low-profile candidates (an 83-year-old first-time candidate and a state-legislative runner-up), while the Democratic primary challengers are progresships unlikely to overcome Larsen's deep incumbency. Under Washington's top-two primary system, the general election will almost certainly feature Larsen vs. a Republican, and district fundamentals indicate a Democratic hold with a large margin.
